description: Puts a bill of materials on a drawing for a view of an assembly (IView.InsertBomTable4 with the view's configuration named, never empty: CADapter measured an empty name making a table with no rows that reports success), in SOLIDWORKS' standard template: top_level (one row per distinct file and configuration among the top-level components; a subassembly is one row), parts_only (parts at every level) or indented. at (sheet mm) puts its anchor corner there; at the sheet format's bill of materials anchor point when absent. Checked by reading the table's cells back, not by SOLIDWORKS' answer: one row per distinct component file and configuration at the level asked, each with the quantity assembly.components counts for it (suppressed components are not counted), in any order; a table with no rows is verification_failed; the model is unchanged. The view's configuration must be the assembly's active one, which assembly.components reads (activate it with configuration.activate). Otherwise the table is deleted again (rolled back). Waits, changing nothing (busy, user_editing), while the user edits a view's sketch or the sheet format (sheet_format: true) or has a command open. After the user exits a view's sketch, SOLIDWORKS keeps that view activated and changes keep waiting until the user lets go of it: ask them to double-click the sheet outside every view.

document.description: The drawing: its title, its full path, or its file name with the extension (e.g. part.SLDPRT, part.SLDDRW), which picks exactly that document. A name several open documents share is refused with the candidates. The active document when absent.

view.description: The view of the assembly the bill lists: a reference (r1.view.…) or its name (Drawing View1).

kind.description: top_level, parts_only or indented; top_level when absent.

x.description: Mm to the right of the sheet's lower-left corner.

y.description: Mm above the sheet's lower-left corner.

at.description: Where the table's anchor corner goes, sheet mm. The sheet format's bill of materials anchor point when absent.

anchor.description: Which corner of the table is at at (or the format's anchor point): top_left, top_right, bottom_left or bottom_right; top_left when absent.
